headline: Researchers Used a Public OpenAI Model to Build a $250,000 Chrome Full-Chain Exploit in Six Days
summary: XBOW researchers used the public GPT-5.6 Sol model to chain three unknown Chrome bugs into a full‑chain exploit that runs code on Windows when a page loads, prompting Google to patch the bugs.
whyItMatters: It shows AI can accelerate creation of powerful browser exploits.
recommendedAction: Update Chrome to the latest version immediately.

headline: AI-Found Linux Kernel Flaw Gives Local Users Root, and Can Break a Guest Out to the Host
summary: A flaw in Linux’s vhost subsystem (CVE‑2026‑74580, named Vghost) allows local users to gain root and enables a virtual machine to write to host memory, potentially hijacking the host.
whyItMatters: It threatens the integrity of Linux hosts and virtualized environments.
recommendedAction: Apply the forthcoming kernel patches as soon as they are available.

headline: Hirudo Android malware replaces banking apps to evade security checks
summary: The Hirudo Android malware replaces legitimate banking apps with modified versions that disable security checks, stealing users' bank account credentials.
whyItMatters: It enables large‑scale financial credential theft.
recommendedAction: Install reputable mobile security software and avoid unknown app sources.

headline: Hirudo Android Trojan Uses Patched Banking Apps to Bypass Their Built-In Security Checks
summary: The Hirudo trojan replaces eight Indonesian banking apps with patched versions that bypass built‑in security checks, facilitating credential theft.
whyItMatters: It represents a new escalation in mobile financial fraud.
recommendedAction: Monitor banking app integrity and use security solutions on Android devices.

headline: An AI Agent Found a Critical OTP Bypass in Production. The Attack Was the Easy Part.
summary: An AI pentesting agent discovered a critical authentication bypass on a major insurer’s production site, allowing the attacker to choose the destination of the one‑time passcode.
whyItMatters: The flaw could let attackers hijack user accounts.
recommendedAction: Review and harden OTP delivery mechanisms immediately.

headline: Four-Byte Write and Timing Bug Let Researchers Run Code in Windows SmartScreen Enclave
summary: Researchers exploited a four‑byte write and timing bug to execute code inside the Windows SmartScreen VBS enclave that protects anti‑phishing secrets.
whyItMatters: Compromising the enclave undermines a core Windows security component.
recommendedAction: Install the upcoming Windows update that addresses the bug.

headline: Microsoft: Recent Windows updates may trigger Remote Desktop failures
summary: Microsoft confirmed that recent Windows updates can prevent non‑admin users from connecting via Remote Desktop when the Administrator protection feature is enabled.
whyItMatters: It may disrupt remote management and support workflows.
recommendedAction: Check RDP settings or defer the updates until a fix is released.
